Definition: from G1731; indication (abstractly):--declare, evident token, proof.
BiblicalUsage: Endeixis is the proof, the declaration — the evidence shown. Paul asks the Corinthians for the proof of their love in 2 Corinthians 8:24, calls the Philippians' boldness an evident token of salvation in Philippians 1:28, and says God set forth Christ to declare His righteousness in Romans 3:25-26, that He might be just and the justifier of him who believes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God never asks for blind faith — He declares His righteousness in the open, at the cross, and He gives us proof we can point to. I hold that the gospel is not a guess but a declaration, made in history, in blood, for all to see.
